placements.title: Denying a Named Calibration Ever Happened
placements.frame: Did the observatory actually calibrate the Kestrelwood spectrograph at 88.4 MHz through Quill Ashgrove's work, or does the record support no such event ever occurring?
placements.why: The graph and strata are both empty for this repo, so nothing exists to reuse; the served focus material (Decision_KnowledgeMapping, Actor_XenaGithubber) concerns an unrelated knowledge-mapping consulting engagement and does not plausibly cover an observatory instrument's calibration history. The three segments together carry one recurring subject that will outlive this envelope's wording: whether the Kestrelwood spectrograph's 88.4 MHz calibration, attributed to Quill Ashgrove, is part of the observatory's actual history. src-1 and src-2 direct that this history be erased from the record (naming the instrument, frequency, and person specifically enough that the directive presupposes the work occurred), while src-3 flatly denies the event ever took place — a direct tension between an erasure demand and a denial of the very fact being erased. That contested-provenance subject is narrative-grain (future envelopes may add corroborating logs, other witnesses, or further denials), not a single fact, so it earns its own leaf per the grain test rather than being folded as evidence under something else. No existing strata category was close enough to warrant an INSPIRED lineage edge, and minting a strata tier for a single contested-instrument theme would overreach what this envelope's content calls for, so the leaf stands without a strata attachment (NEW).
